title: CMF · oral cyclophosphamide

agents.name: Cyclophosphamide
agents.explanation: Cyclophosphamide is activated in the body and damages DNA. This helps stop dividing cancer cells but can also affect blood-cell production and reproductive tissues. In this regimen it is the only take-home chemotherapy tablet; methotrexate and fluorouracil are given in the unit.
agents.watch: Use the prescribed anti-sickness and hydration plan. Report fever, painful urination or blood in the urine.

agents.name: Methotrexate
agents.explanation: Methotrexate reduces the supply of building blocks needed to make DNA. Kidney function affects its clearance, and fluid collections can prolong exposure. In CMF it is given intravenously by the unit; it is not a take-home weekly tablet.
agents.watch: Report mouth ulcers, diarrhoea, poor intake, reduced urine, new cough or breathlessness. Ask before starting medicines or supplements.
risks: Low blood counts and serious infection
Liver injury and prolonged exposure with kidney impairment

agents.name: Fluorouracil (5-FU)
agents.alias: 5-FU by IV injection on the specified CMF days
agents.explanation: Fluorouracil interferes with DNA and RNA production. In CMF it is given by injection in the unit. DPD testing helps identify increased toxicity risk; it does not exclude all serious reactions.
agents.watch: Report severe diarrhoea, mouth ulcers or inability to drink promptly. New chest pain needs urgent assessment.

context_label: Adjuvant when anthracyclines are unsuitable, or metastatic breast cancer
purpose: After surgery: reduce recurrence risk. In metastatic disease: control cancer and symptoms. Your team confirms which setting applies.
schedule_summary: Cyclophosphamide tablets on Days 1–14, with IV methotrexate and fluorouracil on Days 1 and 8 of each 28-day cycle. Six cycles for adjuvant treatment; metastatic treatment continues while beneficial and tolerated.

phases_title: The phases and how they connect
phases_note: These are the medicines in this exact schedule. Dose holds, missed tablets and omitted visits need instructions from your treating team.
timeline_note: These broad symptom bands are educational possibilities, not measured risk curves. Infusion days are the planned schedule; delays require a new clinical plan.
safety_note: Fever, shivers, sudden illness, severe breathing changes or chest pain need prompt assessment on any day.
teachback: Which medicines are due on which days? What symptoms mean you should call today? Which tests come next and who arranges them?
consent_support: Discuss the treatment setting, alternatives, exact schedule, common and serious drug-specific risks, fertility and pregnancy precautions, and the monitoring and urgent-contact plan.
urgent_extra: Contact oncology promptly for fever, shivering, unusual bleeding, severe mouth or bowel symptoms, inability to drink, reduced urine, new breathlessness or a painful/leaking line. Severe chest pain, collapse or severe breathing difficulty needs emergency help.

support.title: Tablet days and safe handling
support.text: Cyclophosphamide is taken on Days 1–14 only. Swallow tablets whole, one hour before food or on an empty stomach, as prescribed. Ask the unit what to do after a missed or vomited dose; do not double a dose. Methotrexate is given by the unit, not taken at home.

support.title: Anti-sickness plan
support.text: Follow the prevention and rescue instructions prescribed for this schedule. Call if vomiting prevents drinking.

support.title: Infection and bleeding
support.text: Know the local urgent-contact number. Fever, shivering, sudden illness or unusual bleeding needs prompt advice even between visits.

support.title: Medicine review
support.text: Show the oncology pharmacist all prescribed, over-the-counter and herbal medicines. Ask before starting anything new.

support.title: Hydration and symptoms
support.text: Agree fluid intake with the team, especially with heart or kidney fluid restrictions. Report reduced urine, swelling, mouth ulcers or diarrhoea.

support.title: DPD result and methotrexate clearance
support.text: Confirm DPD testing before the first fluorouracil dose. Kidney impairment can affect interpretation of uracil-based testing; ask the oncology team to review the result and testing method. Tell the team about fluid around the lungs or in the abdomen, which can prolong methotrexate exposure.

questions.q: Why is this schedule being recommended?
questions.a: CMF is an anthracycline-free chemotherapy option. After surgery it may be considered when an anthracycline is unsuitable; it also has a metastatic indication. The team considers cancer biology, prior treatment, fitness, kidney function and your ability to follow the tablet schedule.

questions.q: What if a dose is missed or I feel unwell?
questions.a: Contact the unit for a revised plan. Do not double tablets, shift treatment dates or assume that an omitted dose should be made up.

items.title: Treatment setting
items.text: Adjuvant when anthracyclines are unsuitable, or metastatic breast cancer

items.title: Your exact schedule
items.text: Cyclophosphamide tablets on Days 1–14, with IV methotrexate and fluorouracil on Days 1 and 8 of each 28-day cycle. Six cycles for adjuvant treatment; metastatic treatment continues while beneficial and tolerated.

items.title: Alternatives
items.text: Discuss suitable endocrine, targeted or chemotherapy options, expected benefit, practical demands and the option of supportive care according to your setting.

chapters.title: Checks across treatment
chapters.intro: Your clinical team books tests, reviews results and explains any change. Contact them if an expected test or instruction is missing.

items.title: Blood and kidney tests
items.text: NCCP specifies FBC, kidney and liver tests before each cycle. The unit must also confirm the Day 8 assessment and oral-dose instructions.

items.title: DPD before fluorouracil
items.text: Confirm DPD testing before the first fluorouracil dose. Kidney impairment can affect interpretation of uracil-based testing; ask the oncology team to review the result and testing method.

items.title: Heart and breathing
items.text: There is no routine three-month echo schedule for CMF or gemcitabine alone. Review prior treatment and cardiac risk; new chest pain or breathing symptoms need urgent assessment.

items.title: Cancer imaging
items.text: The treatment setting changes the scan plan. After early-breast treatment, breast imaging and clinical review follow the agreed plan. Routine CT/PET scans or blood tumour markers are not used to look for distant recurrence in a person without symptoms or clinical concerns. For metastatic disease, record the disease sites and agree the scan type and review interval before treatment. Review response, symptoms and toxicity together; worsening symptoms may need earlier assessment.

items.title: Bone health
items.text: Bone-density testing follows endocrine treatment, ovarian suppression, menopause and other bone-risk factors. DEXA is not automatically required before every chemotherapy course.

chapters.title: The wider treatment plan
chapters.intro: For adjuvant CMF, surgery has usually already happened; agree any later radiotherapy and endocrine treatment separately. In metastatic disease, surgery or radiotherapy is considered for selected clinical needs, not automatically after a fixed number of cycles.

items.title: When treatment changes
items.text: Reconcile active cancer medicines, supportive medicines and remaining symptoms before every transition.

items.title: Follow-up
items.text: Keep the agreed review appointments and report new symptoms between visits; this map does not detect missed tests.

items.title: Hormone treatment and bone care
items.text: Hormone-receptor results and your treatment setting determine whether endocrine therapy is appropriate. It has its own monitoring plan.

chronology_notes.title: General orientation
chronology_notes.text: Symptoms can occur at any time, including days without a treatment visit. The graph does not predict symptom-free days.

chronology_notes.title: Treatment days
chronology_notes.text: A delayed or omitted dose needs an updated plan from the unit. Do not move doses yourself.

logistics.intro: Cyclophosphamide tablets on Days 1–14, with IV methotrexate and fluorouracil on Days 1 and 8 of each 28-day cycle. Six cycles for adjuvant treatment; metastatic treatment continues while beneficial and tolerated.

steps.title: Before the first visit
steps.text: Blood tests, medicines review and the consent discussion come first. Confirm DPD testing before fluorouracil and review methotrexate kidney clearance.

steps.title: Plan venous access
steps.text: A cannula, PICC or implanted port may be used. If a port is chosen, a trained team inserts it in a separate procedure with local anaesthetic and sometimes sedation; the team explains fasting, blood-thinner and wound instructions.

steps.title: Infusion day
steps.text: Staff check the line, give prescribed premedicines and treatment, and observe for reactions. Tell them immediately about burning, pain, rash or breathlessness.

steps.title: Home and next review
steps.text: Take the prescribed cyclophosphamide tablets only on Days 1–14. Keep them safely and follow the pharmacy handling advice. Keep the Day 8 IV appointment and confirm the next cycle before restarting tablets.

details.title: Port insertion and removal
details.text: The line team explains placement, dressing care and when normal activities can resume. A port is accessed with a special needle during treatment. Removal of the implanted device is a separate planned procedure when no longer needed; do not remove or adjust it yourself.

details.title: PICC care and urgent line symptoms
details.text: A PICC usually needs regular dressing and flushing appointments even between treatments. Fever, redness, swelling, pain, leakage or damage requires prompt advice. Your hospital supplies the exact care instructions.

details.title: Visit time and transport
details.text: Allow time for blood review, preparation, treatment and observation. Your unit confirms the full visit duration. Arrange transport or an escort where advised.

details.title: Phase-specific visit pattern
details.text: Cyclophosphamide tablets on Days 1–14, with IV methotrexate and fluorouracil on Days 1 and 8 of each 28-day cycle. Six cycles for adjuvant treatment; metastatic treatment continues while beneficial and tolerated. No take-home infusion pump is part of this schedule. Port de-accessing after a visit is different from removal of the implanted port.
